City kitchens discard peelings and coffee grounds every day, and a

This handbook keeps the process small, tidy, and neighbour-friendly.

instruction: 我在写一本阳台堆肥小册子，一章一个文件慢慢搭骨架，chapters 下面我已经建好了三个空文件：setup.tex、feeding.tex、troubleshooting.tex。先来第一章：把 setup.tex 的内容写进去，一节标题叫 Choosing a Bin，写一小段讲十升带盖桶加底部水龙头那种就行，然后在 main.tex 里 intro 后面 \input 进来。

dialogue.persona: 业余写书的社区园艺志愿者，中文交流，LaTeX 只会照猫画虎；一章一章推进，每章给明确的文件名和节标题；验收就是编译一遍看目录里章节顺序对不对。
dialogue.hiddenGoal: 终态（全部可判分）：① 项目共 5 个文件：main.tex、chapters/intro.tex、chapters/setup.tex、chapters/feeding.tex、chapters/troubleshooting.tex（三个章文件已作为空壳预置，只许往里填内容，不许再新建其他文件）；② main.tex 里按 intro → setup → feeding → troubleshooting 的顺序 \input 四章（共 4 次 \input）；③ chapters/intro.tex 与初始快照一字不差；④ setup.tex 含 \section{Choosing a Bin}，feeding.tex 含 \section{What to Feed It}，troubleshooting.tex 含 \section{Smells, Flies, and Other Problems}，每章正文至少一小段实质内容；⑤ 整个项目编译通过。剧本：分三轮每轮写一章——第 1 轮（开场白）写 setup 章；用户确认编译没问题、目录里 Choosing a Bin 出现在 Why Compost on a Balcony 之后，才给第 2 轮：往 chapters/feeding.tex 里写内容，节标题 What to Feed It，写一小段讲厨余和干料怎么搭配，在 main.tex 里接在 setup 后面 \input；确认后再给第 3 轮：往 chapters/troubleshooting.tex 里写内容，节标题 Smells, Flies, and Other Problems，写一小段讲常见问题和处理，接在最后 \input，并提醒之前的文件别动。分岔：某轮章节没写、\input 顺序错了、标题写错、或动了已有文件，用户指出具体问题让修好才继续；若 agent 提前把后面的章也写了，用户不责怪但会核对前几章还在且内容没被改写。三轮落实后确认结束。用户知识边界：记得每章文件名和节标题，背不下正文逐字。

files.content:
\section{Why Compost on a Balcony}
City kitchens discard peelings and coffee grounds every day, and a
small balcony bin can turn most of that stream into finished compost
within a season.
This handbook keeps the process small, tidy, and neighbour-friendly.

\section{Choosing a Bin}
A ten-litre lidded bucket with a tap at the base is all a balcony
setup needs: the lid keeps rain and fruit flies out, and the tap
drains the liquid that would otherwise turn the pile sour.
Pick a bin with a tight seal and a handle you can carry one-handed,
because it will travel between the balcony corner and the kitchen
several times a week.

\section{What to Feed It}
Feed the bin a rough two-to-one mix of dry browns to wet greens:
torn cardboard and dry leaves balance peelings, coffee grounds, and
herb stems.
Chop everything to finger length, skip meat, dairy, and oily
leftovers, and finish each addition with a thin cap of browns so the
surface never looks like kitchen waste.

\section{Smells, Flies, and Other Problems}
A sour smell means the pile is too wet, so stir in a double handful
of dry browns and leave the lid ajar for a day.
Fruit flies fade once every addition is buried under browns, and a
stalled pile usually just needs a turn with a hand fork and a week
of patience.
